messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: sudden KV cache fragmentation -> increased GPU->CPU paging in us-west-2. Affected model variants: awq-3b-int8, gptq-7b-quant. Spike in token latency and a handful of token timeouts. On-call: @Devon, please ack and triage.

Devon (oncall): acked. I see paging spikes on the runtime dashboards and elevated swap I/O. Pulling logs now.

Marta (eng-runtime): noted. We merged a kernel-selector tweak in last deploy that broadened AWQ kernel rollout; initial hypothesis: AWQ allocator is producing larger fragmented KV allocations for certain sequence length patterns.

Jia (eng-ml): we enabled AWQ fallback for some GPTQ models last week to improve throughput. Sending the diff in case it helps: `git show origin/main~3 -- src/runtime/kernel_selector.py`

Leo (sre): paging metrics: node-swap-usage +32% over baseline on the serving fleet; 99p latency for affected routes up 4-6x. No container OOMs yet but tail latency is killing SLA. Suggest immediate mitigations: throttle continuous batching and disable AWQ kernel on affected model family.

Sophie (support): Customer impact: Support queue has 3 tickets flagged P1s citing >5s token latencies. Two enterprise customers reported degraded UX; one is on a dedicated Dedicated capacity cluster in us-west-2. I'll prepare an initial customer ping. :phone:

Aly (product-ops): I'll coordinate comms. If we expect a rollback window, what ETA?

Devon (oncall): Proposed live mitigation steps (fast):
1) Push a control-plane hotfix to set `runtime.disable_awq_kernel=true` for awq-3b-int8 and gptq-7b-quant — quick toggle, no model re-upload.
2) Reduce continuous_batch config for impacted routes: `continuous_batch.max_tokens: 2048 -> 512`.
3) Lower kv_cache.evict_threshold from `0.6 -> 0.45` to force earlier eviction.
4) Put traffic rule to route heavy tail traffic to gptq-compat variant.

Devon (oncall): CLI snippets for the hotfix (running now):
```bash
# set runtime flag on route group
redwoodctl routes update --route-group awq-3b --set "runtime.disable_awq_kernel=true" --dry-run=false

# shorten cont-batch tokens
redwoodctl config patch --path /routes/awq-3b/continuous_batch/max_tokens --value 512

# kv eviction threshold change
redwoodctl config patch --path /global/kv_cache/evict_threshold --value 0.45
```

IncidentBot: Deploy started: rollout id r-98765 by Devon. Canary -> 5% traffic.

Marta (eng-runtime): I pushed a lightweight KV diagnostic to the canary nodes to dump per-model KV page counts. Quick helper: run on node: 
```python
# /opt/redwood/bin/kv_inspect.py --model awq-3b --dump-pages --json | jq '.pages | length'
```
Expect to see larger-than-normal page counts if fragmentation is occurring.

Jia (eng-ml): also pin kernel selector for the canary to `stable-gemm-v2` so AWQ allocations are avoided while we observe.

Devon (oncall): Canary results (5% traffic): paging I/O down ~60% on canary nodes, 99p latency for canary routes back to baseline. Rolling to 30% now.

Sophie (support): Sent interim note to impacted customers: "We're investigating elevated latency tied to low-level inference allocator behavior; short-term mitigations in progress. We'll follow up with timeline." A couple of customers acknowledged, one asked for a timeline to full restore.

Aly (product-ops): Marking incident as "active mitigation" in tracker and preparing an executive blurb.

Devon (oncall): Rolling to 100% now — monitoring.

IncidentBot: Rollout r-98765 progressed: 30% -> 100% in ~00:18:40.

Devon (oncall): Full roll complete. Observed fleet-wide drop in paging and swap I/O; 99p latencies returned to normal for the affected routes. No further token timeouts observed in last 5m.

Marta (eng-runtime): Post-mortem notes to capture: root likely the kernel-selector diff that widened AWQ kernel eligibility for sequences with many short prefixes; AWQ allocator uses larger granularity pages which increases fragmentation under our KV layout and makes evict thresholds ineffective. Need better sim tests.

Jia (eng-ml): Action items from ML side: pin awq rollout until we have KV footprint simulations; add regression test that runs kernel-selector combinations over synthetic long-short prefix workloads. I'll open PRs today.

Leo (sre): Follow-ups from SRE: add a runtime metric for per-model KV page count and a paging alarm (swap throughput threshold). Also make cont-batch max_tokens adjustable per-deployment via runtime flags for faster mitigation.

Devon (oncall): Handing off follow-up and postmortem ownership to @Leo. I'll attach rollout diffs and canary logs to the incident.

Leo (sre): Ack handoff. I'll own the 48h watch and the postmortem write-up. Tentative RCA: quant path kernel-selection -> allocator fragmentation -> elevated KV pages -> paging -> tail latency.

Sophie (support): I'll follow up with the 3 impacted customers and share the mitigation summary + ETA for postmortem.

IncidentBot: Incident resolved. Duration: 00:42:16. Severity: S2 (partial degraded service for subset of customers). Follow-up tasks assigned: `ML: pin & tests (Jia)`, `Runtime: KV metrics + kernel guard (Marta)`, `SRE: paging alarm + postmortem (Leo)`, `Support: customer follow-ups (Sophie)`.

Devon (oncall): Closing thread for now, leaving logs and rollout ids in the incident tracker. If paging reappears, reopen and escalate. :white_check_mark:
